sub_answers.text: Richard James DeMont was stripped of his 400-meter freestyle Olympic gold medal after his post-race urinalysis tested positive for traces of the banned substance ephedrine contained in his prescription asthma medication, Marax [d11321867s0p0][d36836906s4p0]. The United States Olympic Committee recognized his gold medal performance in 2001, but the International Olympic Committee had refused to restore the medal as of 2017 [d36836906s4p0].

sub_answers.text: Her 100-metre freestyle relay split times were faster than the individual 100-metre freestyle gold medalist, which earned her the honour of swimming in the final of the medley relay despite not competing in the individual 100- and 200-metre freestyle events [d901542s4p0]. Her lead-off 200-metre freestyle split in the 4×200-metre freestyle relay was recorded as the then fourth-fastest time in history (1:57.06), demonstrating a relay lead-off performance that exceeded contemporaneous individual results [d901542s4p0].

sub_answers.text: She won the 50-metre freestyle at the 2005 World Aquatics Championships in 24.59 and took silver in the 100-metre butterfly (57.37) at the same meet [d901542s4p0]. She was part of gold-medal relay teams in the 4×100-metre freestyle (3:37.22) and 4×100-metre medley (3:57.47) and won silver in the 4×200-metre freestyle (7:54.00) at the 2005 World Championships [d901542s4p0]. She recorded a lead-off 200-metre freestyle time of 1:57.06 in that 4×200 final, then the fourth-fastest ever for the event [d901542s4p0]. She lowered the 100-metre short course freestyle world record to 51.70 at the Australian Short Course Championships and set a short-course 200-metre freestyle world record of 1:53.29 at the 2005 FINA World Cup stop in Sydney [d901542s4p0]. She regained the long-course 100-metre freestyle world record with a time of 53.42 on 31 January 2006 and later lowered it again to 52.88 on 27 March 2008 [d901542s4p0].

sub_answers.text: Barbara Krause won Olympic gold medals in the 100 m and 200 m freestyle and in the 4×100 m freestyle relay at the 1980 Summer Olympics in Moscow [d11285120s0p0]. Barbara Krause was an eight-time world record holder during her career [d11285120s0p0]. Libby Trickett won gold in the 50-metre freestyle and golds in the 4×100-metre freestyle relay and 4×100-metre medley relay at the 2005 World Aquatics Championships in Montreal, and silver in the 4×200-metre freestyle relay at the same meet in July 2005 [d901542s4p0]. Libby Trickett recorded a lead-off 200-metre freestyle split of 1:57.06 in the 4×200-metre freestyle relay final at the 2005 World Championships and finished 2005 ranked number one in the world in both the 100- and 200-metre freestyle [d901542s4p0].
